headline: Bus fares up 17 paisa/km after fuel hike; launch, truck fares rise before govt nod
summary: Following a Tk 20/litre increase in diesel, octane, petrol, and kerosene prices, bus fares have been officially adjusted, while launch and truck operators have already started charging higher rates, impacting passengers and traders.
details: Following a Tk 20 per litre hike in retail prices of diesel, octane, petrol, and kerosene, bus fares have been officially raised. Long-distance bus fares increased from Tk 2.23 to Tk 2.40 per kilometre, while Dhaka and Chattogram metropolitan area fares rose from Tk 2.53 to Tk 2.70 per kilometre.

However, some launch and freight operators have already increased fares and charges before any government-approved revision. Passengers at Sadarghat reported higher launch fares depending on the route and seat type.

For instance, a deck ticket from Dhaka to Bhola, normally Tk 300-350, was charged Tk 400. On the Dhaka-Barishal route, deck fares rose from Tk 300 to Tk 350, and single-cabin fares from Tk 1,000 to Tk 1,200.

Truck fares have also seen an increase, with drivers reporting significant additional costs per trip. At Benapole land port, disputes over charges between drivers and traders have been reported since the fuel price hike.

Launch owners stated they could not continue operating at a loss after the fuel price increase and plan to submit a new fare proposal. Truck and lorry fares are expected to be fixed within the week after discussions with district-level owners.
The Road Transport and Bridges Minister had warned truck owners against indiscriminate fare increases. He also stated that launch fares would be reviewed after discussions with owners.

However, some launch and freight operators have already increased fares and charges before any government-approved revision. Passengers at Sadarghat reported higher launch fares depending on the route and seat type.

For instance, a deck ticket from Dhaka to Bhola, normally Tk 300-350, was charged Tk 400. On the Dhaka-Barishal route, deck fares rose from Tk 300 to Tk 350, and single-cabin fares from Tk 1,000 to Tk 1,200.

Truck fares have also seen an increase, with drivers reporting significant additional costs per trip. At Benapole land port, disputes over charges between drivers and traders have been reported since the fuel price hike.

Launch owners stated they could not continue operating at a loss after the fuel price increase and plan to submit a new fare proposal. Truck and lorry fares are expected to be fixed within the week after discussions with district-level owners.

headline: Dengue claims 5 more lives, 1,872 new patients hospitalised in 24 hours
summary: Bangladesh recorded its highest daily dengue admissions this year with 1,872 new patients, bringing the total hospitalisations to 65,499. The death toll for 2024 has now reached 195.
details: Bangladesh has recorded five more dengue deaths in a 24-hour count. Another 1,872 patients were hospitalised during the period, marking the highest number of daily admissions recorded so far this year, health authorities said on Tuesday.
The latest deaths have taken the dengue toll to 195 this year, while the number of hospitalised patients rose to 65,499, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Hospitals in Dhaka North City Corporation admitted 159 new patients, while those in Dhaka South received 191. Elsewhere in Dhaka Division, 391 patients were hospitalised.
Among other divisions, 190 patients were admitted in Barishal, 285 in Chattogram, 316 in Khulna, 105 in Mymensingh, 162 in Rajshahi, 67 in Rangpur and six in Sylhet.

Health authorities have tracked dengue admissions and deaths in Bangladesh since 2000, with 2023 recording the highest hospitalisations at 321,179 and 1,705 deaths. More than 400 people died from dengue last year, while around 102,000 cases were recorded.
